problem: Computing low-rank optimal transport plans is NP-hard and computationally expensive, despite offering better statistical properties than unconstrained optimal transport.
approach: Transport Clustering reduces the low-rank optimal transport problem to a clustering problem performed on correspondences from a full-rank transport solution, yielding polynomial-time approximation algorithms with proven constant-factor guarantees.
contribution: Polynomial-time approximation algorithms achieving (1+γ) approximation for negative-type metrics, (1+γ+√(2γ)) for kernel costs, and (1+γ+ρ) for general metrics.

problem: Standard distributional reinforcement learning does not handle multi-objective settings where multiple rewards must be balanced and risk-sensitivity matters, especially in finance and robotics.
approach: Extend distributional RL to multi-objective settings using vector-risk measures approximated via Knothe-Rosenblatt quantile regression, with a transformer architecture without positional encoding to mitigate artificial ordering.
contribution: Risk-sensitive multi-objective RL framework with convergence guarantees under the distributional Bellman operator and improved performance on MO-Gymnasium benchmarks.

problem: Existing tabular anomaly detection methods require dataset-specific training for each new dataset, incurring high computational cost and poor generalization to unseen domains.
approach: OFA-TAD extracts neighbor-distance patterns as transferable cues across multiple metric spaces via multi-view representations and uses a Mixture-of-Experts scoring network to adaptively fuse anomaly evidence.
contribution: One-for-all generalist framework achieving superior anomaly detection and cross-domain generalizability on 34 datasets from 14 domains after one-time training.

problem: Equivariant Graph Neural Networks face efficiency bottlenecks from explicit construction of geometric features and dense tensor products on every edge, limiting scalability.
approach: E2Former-V2 integrates algebraic sparsity using Equivariant Axis-Aligned Sparsification (EAAS) that converts dense Wigner-6j contractions into sparse operations, implemented via fused Triton kernels for hardware-aware execution.
contribution: Up to 20× higher TFLOPS than standard implementations while preserving predictive accuracy on molecular benchmarks.

problem: Vision-language and robotic action spaces have incompatible metric structures—vision-language is topologically linear and isotropic while action manifolds are non-Euclidean and anisotropic—making direct regression fail.
approach: LAST bridges the heterogeneity via Lie-algebraic mapping that linearizes the action manifold globally and discretizes it locally into schemas and whitened residuals, establishing mathematical isomorphism with isotropic Euclidean space.
contribution: Enhanced convergence and generalizability for Vision-Language-Action models by resolving structural mismatch through Lie-algebraic reconstruction.

problem: Knowledge distillation of Multimodal LLMs relies on static next-token alignment, missing dynamic token interactions that encode essential capabilities for multimodal understanding.
approach: Align-TI introduces two components: IVA aligns on salient visual regions to capture instruction-relevant visual extraction, and TPA aligns sequential token-to-token transition probabilities to capture generative logic.
contribution: 2.6% relative improvement over vanilla KD; distilled Align-TI-2B outperforms LLaVA-1.5-7B by 7.0%, establishing state-of-the-art parameter-efficient MLLM distillation.

problem: Population-Based Training variants have an important hyperparameter controlling steps between updates, but no principled method exists for setting it efficiently.
approach: IPBT automatically adjusts this hyperparameter via restarts that reuse weights and leverage time-varying Bayesian optimization to reinitialize hyperparameters in a task-agnostic way.
contribution: Matches or outperforms 5 prior PBT variants and other HPO algorithms on average across 8 tasks without requiring budget increases or hyperparameter tuning.

problem: Data scheduling for LLM training ignores directional influences and dependencies between samples, yet real-world data exhibits complex interactions that affect training order importance.
approach: D³ formulates sample interactions as a dynamic influence graph with loss-based dependencies and solves constrained optimization over this graph to derive training order respecting information flow.
contribution: Consistent improvements over existing data scheduling methods on pre-training and post-training phases with scalable approximation algorithms.

problem: Neural operators for PDEs struggle to generalize to out-of-distribution test inputs such as novel initial conditions or unseen physics without adapting weights.
approach: Searches over compositions of training operators at test time to approximate unseen dynamics, building on DISCO which provides a dictionary of operators trained across different physics.
contribution: State-of-the-art zero-shot generalization on parameter extrapolation and novel physics combinations while recovering underlying PDE parameters.

problem: Constrained generation in language models faces a tradeoff: greedy decoding enforces validity but distorts distributions, while rejection sampling preserves fidelity but wastes computation.
approach: CARS adaptively prunes invalid continuations by recording them in a trie and subtracting probability mass from future draws, ensuring prefixes proven invalid are never revisited.
contribution: Higher sample efficiency measured in forward passes per valid sample with stronger diversity than greedy constrained decoding and rejection sampling methods.

problem: KL divergence in language model distillation is dominated by the teacher's highest-probability modes, diminishing the influence of lower-probability yet informative components.
approach: Propose a tail-aware divergence that decouples the contribution of top-K predictions from lower-probability predictions while maintaining computational efficiency.
contribution: Competitive performance on mathematical reasoning across datasets with efficient distillation achievable on academic budgets.

problem: Barriers to clinical AI research include difficulty replicating baselines, high computational costs, and required domain expertise, limiting reproducibility and accessibility.
approach: PyHealth 2.0 unifies 15+ datasets, 20+ tasks, 25+ models, and interpretability methods in a single framework supporting multimodal clinical data and diverse computational resources.
contribution: Up to 39× faster processing and 20× lower memory usage enabling work from 16GB laptops; 400+ community members supporting accessible, reproducible healthcare AI.

problem: In modern ML pipelines with abundant pretrained representations and scarce task-specific labels, determining how to effectively use noisy proxy covariates for semi-supervised regression is unclear.
approach: Two-stage estimator learns kernel eigenfeatures from all proxy covariates and fits ridge predictor on labeled data with finite sample bounds accounting for proxy perturbation.
contribution: Fast labeled sample rates recovered when proxy perturbation is controlled; distribution regression as a direct special case with analogous guarantees.

problem: Global embedding geometry metrics exhibit near-zero correlation with compositional binding in vision representations, missing how elements are composed despite capturing which elements are present.
approach: Use input-output Jacobian functional sensitivity rather than geometry-based statistics to track compositional binding capability across 21 vision encoders.
contribution: Functional sensitivity reliably tracks compositional binding while geometry metrics fail; establishes functional sensitivity as critical complementary axis for modeling composite structure.

problem: LLM agents improving at test time through memory updates typically rely on hand-designed prompting rules, making it difficult to align memory updates with multi-step objectives.
approach: MemoPilot trains the memory update process end-to-end using multi-turn GRPO with turn-wise reward signals and context-independent advantage estimation for fine-grained credit assignment.
contribution: Substantially improved test-time learning ranking first in Elo on both Rock-Paper-Scissors (1590) and Limit Texas Hold'em (1762), outperforming Deepseek-V3.2.

problem: Multi-agent RL in large-scale systems with local interactions suffers from credit assignment challenges; global value functions provide weak learning signals while local constructions are difficult to estimate.
approach: Diffusion Value Function (DVF) assigns value to each agent by diffusing rewards over the influence graph with temporal discounting and spatial attenuation, decomposing global value via averaging.
contribution: Up to 11% improvement in average reward across firefighting and distributed computation tasks compared to local and global critic baselines.

problem: Standard fixed activation functions like ReLU, Sigmoid, and Tanh are less expressive than trainable low-degree rational activations for approximating target functions.
approach: Use trainable low-degree rational activation functions that provide exponential improvements in parameter efficiency for approximating functions to target error ε.
contribution: Rational-activation networks require only poly(log log(1/ε)) overhead versus poly(log(1/ε)) for fixed activations; seamlessly integrate into standard architectures.

problem: Insertion-based masked diffusion models use fixed generation schedules not adapted to data, limiting quality for structured sequences where learning data-dependent insertion order could improve generation.
approach: LoFlexMDM learns data-dependent insertion and unmasking rates via learnable order dynamics, generalizing discrete flow matching to variable-length sequences.
contribution: Up to 17.5% improvement in sample quality on De Novo molecule generation and 6.7% on fragment-constrained generation over FlexMDM.

problem: Permutation-equivariant weight-space networks may negatively affect expressive power due to symmetry constraints, yet comprehensive expressivity characterization is missing.
approach: Develop systematic theory proving all prominent permutation-equivariant networks are equivalent in expressive power and establishing universality under mild assumptions on input weights.
contribution: 34% improvement over prior SOTA by modifying existing weight-space models based on theoretical insights into expressivity.

problem: Post-training of reasoning LLMs via SFT and RL shows puzzling behavior where strong SFT underperforms weak SFT in downstream RL, indicating misalignment between SFT and RL objectives.
approach: Analyze complementary roles revealing SFT as structure learner for syntax and RL as content refiner; unified strategy harnesses individual strengths while mitigating weaknesses.
contribution: Deep understanding of post-training methods enabling performance gains beyond data scaling alone on PDF-to-Markdown parsing tasks.

problem: Transferable implicit transfer operators for molecular dynamics have limited out-of-distribution generalization across molecular systems despite efficient sampling capability.
approach: Incorporate protein language model embeddings into coarse-grained TITO models to improve data efficiency and generalization for equilibrium sampling.
contribution: State-of-the-art performance on equilibrium sampling benchmarks for out-of-distribution protein systems including fast-folding proteins.

problem: SFT is optimized in isolation to maximize SFT performance, yet models from stronger SFT checkpoints can underperform weaker ones after identical RL training.
approach: PEAR uses importance sampling to reweight SFT loss at token, block, and sequence levels, correcting SFT-RL mismatch by designing SFT with downstream RL in mind.
contribution: Consistent post-RL performance improvements with pass@8 gains up to 14.6% on AIME-2025 across Qwen and DeepSeek models.

problem: Federated multi-source domain adaptation scales poorly as the number of diverse source domains increases, suffering from high overhead or instability in heterogeneous settings.
approach: GALA couples inter-group discrepancy minimization with linear complexity alongside temperature-controlled centroid-based weighting for dynamic source prioritization.
contribution: State-of-the-art on standard benchmarks; significantly outperforms prior methods in large-scale settings on new Digit-18 benchmark with 18 datasets.

problem: Graph neural networks are widely assumed superior to simpler methods for node representation learning, but the necessity of trainable neighborhood aggregations remains unquestioned.
approach: Fixed Aggregation Features (FAFs) transform graph learning into tabular problems using training-free aggregation, then apply well-established tabular classifiers.
contribution: MLPs trained on FAFs rival or outperform state-of-the-art GNNs on 12 of 14 benchmarks, challenging assumptions about deep GNN necessity.

problem: LLM editing methods successfully change targeted behavior but risk corrupting general capabilities through proxy/reward hacking, producing degenerate behaviors.
approach: CrispEdit treats capability preservation as explicit constraint using second-order optimization, projecting edits onto low-curvature subspace of capability-loss landscape via Kronecker-factored curvature.
contribution: High edit success with capability degradation below 1% on average, significantly improving over prior editors.

problem: Conventional wisdom attributes model-based RL limitations to long-term prediction errors, yet search can harm performance even with highly accurate models.
approach: Show that mitigating overestimation bias matters more than improving accuracy; using ensemble minimum over value functions effectively addresses bias.
contribution: State-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks by focusing on bias correction rather than accuracy improvement.

problem: Dynamic graphs exhibit tightly entangled spatiotemporal evolution causing representation drift from structural incompleteness and signal distortion from noise, weakening DGNN robustness.
approach: DeR-Mamba decouples multi-domain entanglement via MP-K²alman for spatial decoupling, AFDM for frequency-domain decoupling, and self-consistent state-space for temporal decoupling.
contribution: Superior robustness on benchmarks with adversarial attacks through principled decoupling of spatiotemporal evolution.

problem: Cross-domain offline RL with heterogeneous source datasets faces value misassignment where values align but assignments mislead filtering, degrading performance.
approach: V2A integrates dynamics alignment, value alignment, and value assignment using temporally-consistent modality representation learning and modality-aware advantage learning.
contribution: Significantly outperforms baselines under general heterogeneous cross-domain offline RL settings.

problem: Sampling from unnormalized densities via diffusion models requires significant tradeoffs such as restricting priors or relying on unstable optimization schemes.
approach: Generalize matching-based methods as fixed-point iterations rooted in Nelson's relation to learn stochastic transport maps between arbitrary distributions with stable objective.
contribution: Unprecedented sampling scales while preserving mode diversity on complex synthetic densities and high-dimensional molecular benchmarks.

problem: LLM pre-training exhibits two-phase dynamics with fast initial loss drop then slow improvement, but underlying mechanisms remain unclear.
approach: Identify Stability of Singular Distribution (SoSD) where trace-normalized singular value spectrum stabilizes early while parameters evolve; prove growing norms precipitate SoSD threshold.
contribution: Spectral lens for understanding efficient pre-training dynamics; interpret strategies like weight standardization through SoSD modulation ability.

problem: Decision trees and diffusion models appear disparate and disconnected, limiting insights from unified understanding.
approach: Establish mathematical correspondence between hierarchical decision trees and diffusion processes, revealing Global Trajectory Score Matching (GTSM) as shared optimization principle.
contribution: Treeflow achieves competitive generation on tabular data with 2× speedup; dsmtree distills hierarchical logic into neural networks matching teacher within 2%.

problem: Existing QA benchmarks provide explicit evidence, but real-world questions require searching massive data lakes followed by reasoning over multiple heterogeneous sources.
approach: Build LakeQA on heterogeneous ~9.5TB resources from Wikipedia and government data, requiring long-horizon multi-hop reasoning over discovered documents.
contribution: Comprehensive benchmark showing GPT-5.2 achieves only 14.73% exact match, providing realistic testbed for LLM agents that both find and analyze data.

problem: fMRI decoders face performance-fidelity tradeoff where efficient encoders outperform geometrically faithful surface-based models, partly from inefficient surface tokenization and unused anatomy.
approach: NeurIPS reframes anatomical variation from nuisance to predictive signal via Selective ROI Spherical Tokenizer for efficient encoding and Structure-Guided MoE using cortical features.
contribution: State-of-the-art surface decoder performance with dramatic convergence speedup (10 vs 600 epochs) and robust scalability with only 20% data for new subjects.

problem: Sparse autoencoders' role and practical value for analyzing embeddings are debated; their interpretability and utility remain unclear.
approach: Demonstrate SAEs can be understood as topic models, deriving SAE objective as MAP estimator under continuous topic model inspired by LDA.
contribution: More coherent topics than baselines while maintaining diversity; enables large-scale thematic analysis across modalities without retraining.

problem: Knowledge boundaries of LLMs remain unclear; static benchmarks provide limited support for systematic knowledge probing across granularities.
approach: Interactive agentic framework with adaptive exploration policies to systematically extract knowledge, plus three-stage processing pipeline for quality assurance.
contribution: Clear knowledge scaling law where larger models recover more knowledge; identified Pass@1 versus Pass@k tradeoff and distinct knowledge profiles across model families.

problem: Multi-stage 2D+3D open-vocabulary 3D instance segmentation pipelines are prohibitively slow (hundreds of seconds), while pseudo-labeled end-to-end methods rely on fragmented masks.
approach: SpaCeFormer uses proposal-free space-curve transformer with spatial window attention and Morton-curve serialization, paired with SpaCeFormer-3M largest dataset via multi-view clustering.
contribution: 0.12–0.30 seconds per scene (2–3 orders of magnitude faster); 21× higher mask recall than prior methods; 11.1 zero-shot mAP on ScanNet200.

problem: RL for reachability specifications lacks theoretical convergence guarantees and provides limited insight into convergence dynamics.
approach: Build on PAC learning with iteratively refined estimation of unknown MDP parameters; iteratively satisfy PAC conditions to achieve exact optimality in the limit.
contribution: Deeper theoretical insights into convergence dynamics and finite-time near-optimal guarantees; exact optimality achieved asymptotically.

problem: Text-to-image diffusion models struggle with precise text rendering, especially multi-line layouts, dense typography, and long-tailed scripts, requiring costly retraining.
approach: FreeText leverages intrinsic DiT mechanisms: extract token-wise spatial attribution for writing regions via sink-like anchors, inject noise-aligned glyph priors with spectral modulation.
contribution: Training-free plug-and-play framework improving text readability on Qwen-Image, FLUX.1-dev, and SD3 while maintaining semantic alignment and aesthetic quality.

problem: Designing biological sequences faces vast search spaces and limited evaluation budgets; evolutionary approaches ignore sequential dependencies while RL/generative models need large datasets.
approach: IDEAS combines sample efficiency of evolutionary approaches with sequential structure exploitation via mutations guided by explainable models identifying critical motifs.
contribution: 19% acceleration in design across eight continuous-property datasets while maintaining favorable Pareto tradeoff on acceleration, diversity, and novelty.

problem: Foundation models dominate many domains but remain under-explored for time series classification, with existing literature focused on forecasting.
approach: Mantis is a transformer-based foundation model pre-trained on synthetic data via self-supervised contrastive learning with novel token generator unit for effective tokenization.
contribution: State-of-the-art across four diverse dataset collections via enhanced test-time methodology leveraging intermediate representations, self-ensembling, and embedding fusion.
